Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the level of agreement among annotators when labeling or annotating data. IAA can be improved by developing clear and concise annotation guidelines, providing annotator training and feedback, using multiple annotators, and adjudicating disagreements. Best practices for achieving high IAA include pilot testing and refining annotation guidelines, monitoring annotator performance, and using IAA metrics to evaluate annotator consistency.

results.content: # Improving Inter-Rater Reliability for Data Annotation and Labeling. Previously, we’ve looked at what inter-rater reliability (IRR) means in the context of data labeling and why it matters when building fair and consistent AI systems. A Look at How Data Annotators Use Inter-Rater Reliability. ## Use Cases of Improving Inter-Rater Reliability in Annotation. Here, inter-rater reliability helps by indicating the degree of agreement among annotators on such tasks, making it easier to identify unclear guidelines. At Objectways, inter-rater reliability is built into the data annotation process from the beginning. Inter-rater reliability is an important part of producing high-quality labeled data, and at Objectways, we believe in doing more than measuring agreement between annotators. + Inter-rater reliability is a way to measure how consistently different people label or evaluate the same data. * **Why is inter-rater reliability important in data annotation?**. + Inter-rater reliability can be improved by creating clear, detailed labeling guidelines with examples, providing ongoing training and feedback, and using a multi-step review process to catch inconsistencies.

results.title: A Guide to Inter-rater Reliability and Annotator Agreement in AI
results.content: Model Agreement: How Inter-Rater Consistency Shapes Benchmark Reliability. When human annotators disagree, it raises a critical question: how can we trust an AI model trained on that data? But when human annotators disagree, the data becomes unreliable, and so do the benchmarks we use to judge model performance. Inter-rater consistency (IRC) helps measure how much human annotators agree on a task. These benchmarks use labeled data as a reference, and that is where human annotation comes in. Inter-Rater Consistency (IRC) measures the degree of agreement among different human annotators when labeling or judging the same data. Sometimes, an AI model seems to perform better than human annotators. If the benchmark was built on low inter-rater consistency, the model may only be learning to match one version of the label, not the full range of human judgment. Despite strong model performance, gold standards for coding tasks still suffer from inter-rater and annotation inconsistencies.

results.title: Inter-rater agreement for the annotation of neurologic signs and symptoms in electronic health records - PMC
results.content: # Inter-rater agreement for the annotation of neurologic signs and symptoms in electronic health records. We have examined inter-rater agreement for annotating neurologic concepts in clinical notes from electronic health records. Furthermore, more training examples combined with improvements in neural networks and natural language processing should make machine annotators capable of high throughput automated clinical concept extraction with high levels of agreement with human annotators. **Keywords:** natural language processing, annotation, electronic health records, phenotype, clinical concept extraction, inter-rater agreement, neural networks, signs and symptoms. In this paper, we examine inter-rater agreement for text-span identification of neurological concepts in notes from electronic health records. Signs and symptoms (ataxia, fatigue, weakness, memory loss, etc.) were annotated but not disease entities (Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, etc.) Raters annotated the neurologic concepts and ignored laterality and other modifiers (e.g., *arm pain* for *right arm pain*, *back pain* for *severe back pain*, etc.) In addition, annotators tagged each text span with an category label (see Figures 1A,B). The machine annotator (NN) was a neural network that was trained to recognize text spans containing neurology concepts in the electronic health record physician notes. Each annotator identified the text span associated with each sign and symptom and assigned a category label to each annotation (e.g., unigram, bigram, trigram, etc.) Inter-rater agreement (adjusted and unadjusted) was calculated between the three human annotators and the machine annotator (NN). The concordance (unadjusted agreement) for category labels was lower than the inter-rater agreement for text spans which may have been due to factors such as the use of hyphens in the free text of the EHR notes and annotator uncertainty about which types of text spans required the tabular label. Although high throughput phenotyping of electronic health records by manual methods is impractical (13), the manual annotation of free text in electronic health records can be used to train neural networks for phenotyping. Although the inter-rater agreement between human and machine annotators was lower than between human annotators, advances in natural language processing should bring inter-rater agreement between machines and humans closer and make high throughput phenotyping of electronic health records feasible. 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv076 [DOI] [PMC free article] [PubMed] [Google Scholar&author=SJ%20Hebbring&author=M%20Rastegar-Mojarad&author=Z%20Ye&author=J%20Mayer&author=C%20Jacobson&volume=31&publication_year=2015&pages=1981-7&pmid=25657332&doi=10.1093/bioinformatics/btv076&)].

results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA)
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). * Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the consistency among human annotators using metrics such as Cohen’s κ and Krippendorff’s α. Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is the fundamental statistical and methodological construct quantifying consistency among human annotators engaged in labeling, segmenting, or otherwise providing structured judgments over datasets. * Routine reporting of both **inter-** and **intra-annotator agreement**; intra-annotator agreement tracks label stability over time and isolates causes of low IAA due to subjective variance versus ambiguity or guideline inadequacy (Abercrombie et al., 2023). **Worker reliability weighting**: By leveraging inter-annotator and intra-annotator agreement, frameworks such as EffiARA compute annotator reliability scores used to re-weight samples during model training, directly improving downstream classifier performance—especially in low-agreement or subjective tasks (Cook et al., 2024). * **Multi-faceted reporting:** Combine intra-annotator agreement with IAA to dissect stability versus reliability and employ diagnostic matrices that distinguish subjectivity from ambiguity (Abercrombie et al., 2023). 4.
